Once again a happy customer of Mike's! I'm very picky when it comes to rugeliis and Mike helped me select the clone I liked best, which ended up being clone H.

Left to right:
flava rugelii clone H, minor giant Ware Co Clone C (red), and a freebie - flava rugelii Bay Co, Select Clone - so now I have two of the best rugeliis around! I'm really excited to see all of these this growing season.

Untitled by Adam G, on Flickr

I placed an order with Mike in February, and a second order that I just received. Excellent size plants, a great selection, and he was very helpful!

New order:

Wasabi “Mazuma” notice old greenhouse with slats... pot is temporary because I just moved to a new house
postimg.cc/B8jLx6fs

The S. rubra gulfensis Green Giant; already a small giant! Look how fat it is, it’s fatter than any of my other Sarracenia.
postimg.cc/zy35LV4k

And a freebie! It’s a S. flava rubricorpora:
postimg.cc/cvy0DL30

A bag of Sphagnum is looking happy:
postimg.cc/mzGmqKwc

posts.body_html:
Now for my first order-

S. psittacina okee Santa Rosa Co FL, look at this thing’s fins! Grows faster than Calhoun Co FL:

postimg.cc/cKs7Pz5C
postimg.cc/GHyjDGyL

Now is the larger of the two S. psittacina okees I have. S. psittacina okee Calhoun Co FL; please note it is not full size yet. It has a bigger potential size than the Santa Rosa clone (I got that right, right?). The Calhoun grows painfully slowly. Its new pitchers are reddish orange while the Santa Rosa clone has new pitchers that are green. So it would seem that green psittacinas grow faster... to be continued.
postimg.cc/sMP96zmb

This was a free plant and has become one of my favorites. It is S. leucopylla alba “Rod’s favorite x dipped lip.” It’s blinding white, literally shining! lol, actually a bad focus.
postimg.cc/N9F6jHtw
postimg.cc/94JP2Bvp

Slipper orchid vs leucopylla alba:
postimg.cc/fkjM14xY

The calhoun co psittacina is planted with the leucopylla alba. It seemed like a good idea at the time.

Here is a free S. flava cuprea. I’ll have to check on what the exact name of it is, but it looks promising so far.
postimg.cc/JHy5PBYQ

I’m glad I was able to get these plants and the free ones. I like the surprise when you get an extra plant- it makes you wonder what you’ll get!

posts.body_html: I love getting my sarrs from Mike. His library of material is huge, and he’s always excited to chat about them too. Sometimes I just describe basic features I’m looking for and he’ll go and find something that fits, even something as obscure as “something with a long white shaft with a bulbous head”. I’m never disappointed. I’ve even received orders with freebies that are more desirable than the order itself. If I knew that was going to happen, I would have purchased some cheaper plants

posts.body_html:
A quick shout-out to Mike Wang for doing what he does best - produce beautiful Sarracenia!

I've ordered from him 2-3 times over the last few years and he never fails to impress. His selection is huge and his willingness to search for the plant YOU want through his massive collection is admirable.

I ordered 3 plants recently and Mike was kind enough to send a bonus plant. Thanks, Mike! They all arrived in excellent condition and are now planted in my home garden.

I can't recommend Mike enough if you're looking for QUALITY Sarracenia. Happy growing everyone!

-Jeff

posts.body_html:
First time buyer from Mike, and was not disappointed. He’s popular amongst my circle of cultivar enthusiasts, and I’ve seen his plants decorating other’s homes. Mine arrived looking fresh from the greenhouse. Rhizomes all healthy, pitchers neatly pruned, all plants were firm and plump and ready for spring! The selection was amazing, and I found all I was looking for. I have ordered from many other reputable nurseries, and the health of Mikes are amazing in comparison.
There is no guesswork when I say I’ll be back for more.
Much love,
KitsuChi
